name: alpelisib
uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE PIQRAY is indicated in combination with fulvestrant for the treatment of adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, PIK3CA-mutated, advanced or metastatic breast cancer as detected by an FDA-authorized test following progression on or after an endocrine-based regimen. PIQRAY is a kinase inhibitor indicated in combination with fulvestrant for the treatment of adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, PIK3CA-mutated, advanced or metastatic breast cancer as detected by an FDA-authorized test following progression on or after an endocrine-based regimen. ( 1 , 2.1 )
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and efficacy of PIQRAY in pediatric patients have not been established. Animal Toxicity Data In a juvenile toxicity study, daily oral administration of alpelisib to juvenile rats from postnatal day (PND) 7 through PND 70 (approximately equivalent to neonatal through adulthood in humans) resulted in reduced body weights, decreased femur lengths, and adverse effects in the kidney in both sexes and delayed balanopreputial separation in males at 20 mg/kg/day (equivalent to exposure in humans at the recommended dose of 300 mg/day based on AUC). Adverse renal effects included increased vascular/perivascular extracellular matrix deposition in small vessels and tubular degeneration/regeneration in the renal papilla and medulla. The adverse renal effects persisted following a 14-week recovery period. In a 4-week general toxicology study, rats administered alpelisib had growth plate thickening and decreased trabeculae of the knee joint, dentin thinning, and degenerative odontoblasts at the dose of 30 mg/kg/day (approximately 3 times the exposure in humans at the recommended dose of 300 mg/day based on AUC). Dentin thinning/irregular dentin was also observed in the 13-week toxicology study in rats at the high dose of 20 mg/kg/day (equivalent to exposures in humans at the recommended dose of 300 mg/day based on AUC).
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS PIQRAY is contraindicated in patients with severe hypersensitivity to it or any of its components [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)] . Severe hypersensitivity to PIQRAY or to any of its components. ( 4 )
interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Strong CYP3A Inducers : Avoid coadministration. Consider an alternative concomitant drug with no or minimal potential to induce CYP3A. ( 7.1 ) BCRP Inhibitors : Avoid coadministration. If unable to use alternative drugs, closely monitor for increased adverse reactions. ( 7.1 ) 7.1 Effect of Other Drugs on PIQRAY Strong CYP3A Inducer Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A inducers with PIQRAY and consider an alternative concomitant drug with no or minimal potential to induce CYP3A. Alpelisib is a CYP3A substrate [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)] . Coadministration with a strong CYP3A inducer decreases alpelisib concentration [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)] , which may reduce alpelisib effectiveness. BCRP Inhibitors Avoid coadministration of BCRP inhibitors with PIQRAY. If cannot avoid coadministration, monitor for increased adverse reactions. Alpelisib is a BCRP substrate [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)] . Coadministration of PIQRAY with a BCRP inhibitor may increase alpelisib concentration [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)] , which may increase the risk of adverse reaction.
